other_errors_seen: B76 (report only): no spelling of '#pragma frep' works in ref-18, int-20 or 20-F024. The fork parser (clang/lib/Parse/ParsePragma.cpp PragmaFrepHandler::HandlePragma ~1653) accepts exactly '#pragma frep infer' (identifier 'infer' is the only valid option; anything else, e.g. 'frep(infer)', prints 'Error, not a identifier token...' / 'option not recognized' via printf and drops the pragma). So the README spelling IS the intended one. It is then rejected in Sema: ParseStmt.cpp ParsePragmaFrep builds the ParsedAttr with 2 args (pragma name + option), but the Frep attr in clang/include/clang/Basic/Attr.td (~4371) declares 1 EnumArgument and no HasCustomParsing, so Sema::checkCommonAttributeFeatures (SemaAttr.cpp ~1544) reports "'frep' attribute takes one argument". LoopHint (same pattern, 3 declared args, parser passes 4) avoids this with an explicit let HasCustomParsing = 1 in its Attr.td def. Fix belongs in clang-frep-pragma (Attr.td: let HasCustomParsing = 1, or consistent arg count), not in the README. '#pragma clang frep infer' is silently ignored (unknown pragma). Workaround today: --snitch-frep-inference (llc) / -mllvm -snitch-frep-inference.
The fork pragma parser reports errors with printf instead of diagnostics (ParsePragma.cpp 1660/1670/1688, ParseStmt.cpp ParsePragmaFrep, SemaStmtAttr.cpp handleFrepAttr).
